verification.note: Traced at 76d34044c. CollectionDetail.tsx:445-446 passes queuePane={fileId !== null} and visitUntilLeft. Once a file has been opened, TwoPaneLayout.tsx:141-152 keeps the visit after ?file= is cleared (visitStarted.current stays true and wanted = !treeEnabled && besideViewport && visitStarted). TwoPaneLayout.tsx:172-175 clears treeYieldStore when hasFile is false, so yieldState.filePage is false. useTreeVisible.ts:66 therefore skips the visit branch, and useTreeVisible.ts:83-85 calls setEnabled(!enabled). On the first press tree:enabled becomes true and the layout effect clears the visit, but the pane stays visible through `enabled`. On the second press tree:enabled becomes false; the effect's wanted is true again, and treeVisitStore.show (treeVisitStore.ts:32-34, hidden:false) brings the pane back. visible = visitVisible || … (useTreeVisible.ts:58-59) stays true. Every press writes storage and the pane never hides. TreeToggle.tsx:46 calls this toggle, and routeHidesTree (driveViews.ts:74-91) does not hide the button on /collections/ routes. This breaks I13: hiding a pane shown for the visit must not write tree:enabled. A side effect: an odd number of presses leaves the stored setting on after the page is left.

CollectionDetail.queue.test.tsx:82 mocks TreeToggle to () => null. The r7 F8 test (CollectionDetail.queue.test.tsx:617-656) checks only the pane's aria-hidden and that no tree:enabled write happens during navigation; it never presses the button. TwoPaneLayout.queuePane.test.tsx:16 fixes the route params to 'file=f1', and none of its cases passes visitUntilLeft (grep finds visitUntilLeft only in CollectionDetail.tsx and TwoPaneLayout.tsx). No test covers the button on the list, or a pane the reader hid across the ?file= clear.

unspecified_scores.reason: With the tree setting off, opening any file on a collection page from a grid card or link sets queuePane (CollectionDetail.tsx:445) and starts the visit, so the item pane then stays on the collection list. This is consistent with a collection being a queue page and is mostly harmless.
A reader who had a URL sort on the folder listing before pressing Play all finds the listing back in its default sort after ending the queue, and has to pick the sort again.

It needs a queue selection cancelled by the unsaved-changes guard, followed by a later arrival at the same file. That file then starts playing despite Autoplay being off, which is surprising but easy to pause.
Resizing or rotating across md brings a visit pane the reader hid back into view, and one press hides it again.

specification_compliance: I13 is not met on a collection list after ?file= is cleared: the tree button writes tree:enabled:{drive} and cannot hide the pane shown for the visit (F1 confirmed).

I18 (revised SPEC-CORE-082 I8) requires a pane shown for the visit to be hidden and re-shown without a storage write. The code does this only while a file is open, because useTreeVisible.ts:66 tests yieldState.filePage.
regression_risks: Fixing F1 by routing the press to treeVisitStore.toggle whenever visit.active is set must not change the folder-page press, where no visit is active and the press edits the setting.
The visit effect in TwoPaneLayout.tsx:143-152 calls show() again whenever its deps change and the visit is inactive. Any fix that clears the visit on a press will make the pane reappear.
test_coverage: No test presses the tree button on a collection list after ?file= is cleared with the setting off (F2).
The TwoPaneLayout.queuePane tests run only with file=f1 and without visitUntilLeft.
not_verified: I did not run any test or the app. F1 was traced by reading the code only.
I did not check whether ChromeButtons or another host renders TreeToggle at md and wider on the collection route beyond TreeToggle's own guards.
I did not trace the play-intent consumption path (unspecified entry 2) in the queue module.
